newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa launches rand/dollar futures contract.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa launches rand/dollar futures contract.

text.p: The South African Futures Exchange's (Safex) on Wednesday started trading rand/dollar futures, in a further sign of the gradual relaxation of exchange controls.

For the time being trade in the contracts -- which started dealing at 8.30 a.m. (0630 GMT) -- is limited to non-resident clients of Safex members and authorised dealers. But Safex and the authorities aim to open the market over time as capital controls are dismantled.

"The advent of futures on the rand is an important milestone in the evolution of our financial markets and serves to bring South Africa further into the realm of the world's sophisticated economies," the finance ministry said in a statement.

Dealers said volumes traded were likely to be sluggish initially but turnover would pick up as the government pressed on with plans to phase out exchange restrictions, allowing both residents and foreigners to hedge rand currency risks.

South Africa already has a well-established informal rand/dollar forward market but Safex said the new contract would offer the advantages of a standardised, formalised contract on a regulated exchange.
However, the Johannesburg-based electronic exchange faces competition.

The Chicago Mercentile Exchange is also launching a competing dollar/rand product on Wednesday and a third contract was listed recently on FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange, and trades in New York and Dublin.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel, who gave the go-ahead for the futures contract in his March 12 budget, said the launch of the new contracts was a sign of South Africa's reintegration into the world economy.
Speaking in Chicago last week, ahead of the CME's parallel futures launch, Manuel said they were "a very, very exicting part of this globalisation".
The underlying instrument on the futures will be the spot rand/dollar exchange rate, quoted to four decimal places, and contracts will be valued at $100,000 each.

Expiry dates would follow the same cycle as equity contracts -- March, June, September and December -- with expiry prices determined by taking a notional offer to buy and sell from six authorised dealers at the expiry time, followed by the arithmetic average of the middle four rates.
The futures will be cash settled in rand.
Safex will also list options on futures with strike prices at intervals of 0.01 rand/dollar.
